classification.difficultyReason: Combines regular-polygon symmetry with isosceles-triangle angle reasoning in a ten-point star.

content.prompt: Joining every third vertex of a regular decagon gives the star shown below. Find the measure of each of the outermost angles in this star.

spec.description: Regular decagon with horizontal top and bottom edges and leftmost and rightmost vertices. All ten chords joining every third vertex are retained. Decorative cyan fill is omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: Vertices lie at successive 36-degree rotations; star edges connect vertex i to vertex i+3 modulo 10.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers or auxiliary solution lines are shown.

answer.short:
$72^{\circ}$.

Join the centre to a star tip and use the two congruent isosceles triangles.
answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the centre, $A$ a star tip, and $B$ and $C$ the two vertices joined to $A$. Join $O$ to these vertices. Each central angle subtending one decagon side is $\frac{360^{\circ}}{10}=36^{\circ}$, so $\angle AOB=\angle AOC=3\times36^{\circ}=108^{\circ}$.

Since $OA=OB=OC$, the two isosceles triangles give
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAO&=\frac{180^{\circ}-108^{\circ}}{2}\\\angle BAO&=36^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
By symmetry, $\angle OAC=36^{\circ}$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=36^{\circ}+36^{\circ}\\\angle BAC&=72^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Every outermost angle is equal by rotational symmetry.
